rules: Operation identity is DX0's: every id is a feature-exposure-contract.v1.json row id, and hostExecutionClass, answerRail and browserAdmitted equal the joined DX0 row's hostExecutionClass, answerRail and browserExecutable. A divergence is a validation failure requiring a DX0 receiving-owner amendment, never a manifest relabel (no class change happens by moving code).

Every DX0 row with browserExecutable true must appear here admitted (join completeness); BWH0 introduces no operation without a DX0 row, so AC-EXPOSURE traceability holds by construction and DX1 registration obligations attach to the rows that add browser execution, not to this manifest.

browserAdmitted requires the DX0 Portable class plus a baseline-no-isolation compatibility row; crossOriginIsolationRequired and sharedArrayBufferRequired are false on every admitted row, and a true value rejects the admission (BWH0-AC2).

A NativeOnly row may be presented in a browser product only as explicitly selected local-native execution (DX4/DX5 companion route) or as a labelled gap; claiming it browser-executable without a shipped build is rejected (DX0-AC2 lineage).
Every row binds source/project/configuration/profile, execution host and engine version, its completeness state and invalidation/lifetime rules through DX0's ProductReceiptBasis.
portabilityProof.substrateExports records the WASM compiler host's build surface; substrate exports are build facts, not admitted operations (BWH0-AC3).
A compiler-WASM build never proves semantic-host portability (BWH0-AC3); semantic-host claims cite BWH1..BWH6B evidence.

receivingAmendments.rule: amendments are recorded before code; no reverse edges into the product-observability train; combined-graph validation runs after every amendment.
